---
title: "Slide"
subtitle: "Figure-first talks: compose slides like figures, reveal them beat by beat, export one file that plays anywhere"
---

Slide turns project content into talks. A project can hold several **decks**; each deck is a
filmstrip of slides you compose on a stage — and the stage *is* the
[figure editor](figure.qmd): the same tools, the same Inspector, the same
[live plots](../concepts/semantic-plots.qmd). Anything you can do to a figure, you can do to a
slide; figures travel between the two worlds without translation.

# Decks and the filmstrip

The deck list sits above the filmstrip: create (**+ New deck**), duplicate, or remove decks —
each is one readable file in the project. The filmstrip shows live thumbnails: drag to
reorder, duplicate or delete from a thumb, **+ Add slide** for a new slide (layouts seed
starter text — title, section, two-column, or *blank* for a clean stage), and **+ Preset**
inserts a slide from your machine-global **slide preset library** (save any slide there from
the Slide panel — its animation, background, and media travel with it).

The right rail holds the **Slide panel** (name, per-slide **background**, transition, speaker
notes) and the **Deck panel**: the **theme** — seven built-ins from *Flux Dark* through *Flux
Light*, *Paper*, *Midnight*, *Slate*, *Sepia*, and *Contrast* — and the **stage size** (16:9,
4:3, 16:10). **Ctrl+Shift+B** hides the whole rail, and both rails resize by dragging their
inner edge (the filmstrip too; **Ctrl+B** hides it when no text is selected).

# Beats

Animation is built around **beats**: each slide reveals or changes things step by step, the
way you'd build an argument. Beat 0 is *Start* — the slide at rest; each further beat is one
press of the advance key. A beat can also play **with** the previous one, or **auto** after a
delay, so multi-part builds land as one gesture.

The canvas is **beat-faithful**: it always shows the slide *as it exists at the selected
beat*, and editing simply changes what you see — edit at beat 3 and you're shaping beat 3's
state; edit at *Start* and you're shaping the resting slide.

# The Animator

**Animate ⏱** opens the animator dock. Beats appear as chips; the expanded beat shows its
**tracks** as lanes on a millisecond ruler — drag a lane to retime it, drag its right edge for
duration, drag it onto another beat to move it (**Alt** copies), and group related lanes into
collapsible boxes. The **Properties** mini-pane edits the selected track: preset, start,
duration, easing and influence, and — for staggered tracks — order and direction.

To animate something: select it on the stage (**Ctrl+click** drills to a plot *part* — a
single series can animate on its own), then

- **Ctrl+Shift+A** — add an **appearance** (enter),
- **Ctrl+Shift+D** — add a **disappearance** (exit),
- **Ctrl+Shift+T** — add a **transform** (see below).

Each element type gets a sensible default (text fades and rises, shapes pop, lines and paths
draw on), and **✨ Auto-animate** builds a whole entrance sequence for a selected plot from its
anatomy — series draw on, points stagger in. **▶ Preview** plays the build on the stage;
**☆ Library** holds your saved animation presets and multi-track templates.

## Appearances

The preset menu covers entrances (**fade**, **fadeRise**, **popIn**, **growBaseline**,
**drawOn**, **writeOn**), exits (**fadeOut**, **popOut**, **drawOff**, **wipeOut**), emphasis
(**highlight**, **dim**), **stagger** — members of a group or points of a series arrive in
sequence, ordered by position or index, from either end or the center — and **countUp**, which
tweens a number in a text element ("n = 1,247" counts up in place). Draw-on/off expose full
**trim path** control (direction, anchor, single/both-ends/middle-out, partial windows), and
wipes pick their direction.

## Transforms and morphs

A **transform** tweens an element into a *different version of itself* between two beats. Add
one and its **t₂** endpoint checks out onto the canvas: edit the object with every ordinary
tool — move it, resize it, recolor it, rewrite its text, hide plot parts — then **Escape**.
The animator records the difference and plays it as motion; the lane shows **t₁ — t₂**
handles, and clicking either endpoint re-opens it for editing. Chained transforms across beats
compose, colors blend perceptually, rewritten numbers digit-tween.

For plots, a transform can also carry a **data morph**: pick a target plot with **⇄ Morph**
(or the track's *data morph* dropdown) and one chart tweens into the other — axes, series and
all. Morphs are for structurally matched pairs (same series, same axes family); incompatible
targets are flagged rather than mangled.

**🎥 Zoom** adds a camera move to the selected element (**⤢ Reset** pulls back) — build-a-tour
zooms without leaving the beat model.

## Cascading tracks

Select several tracks and press **Ctrl+Shift+C**: the same [cascade](figure.qmd#cascade)
popover, over animation — stagger **start**, **duration**, **per-item stagger**, or easing
**influence** in even steps across the selection. Five drawOns starting 120 ms apart is one
gesture, not arithmetic.

# Presenting

**F5** presents from the start (**Shift+F5** from the current slide). Arrow keys and **Space**
advance beats (**Shift+arrows** jump whole slides), a typed **number + Enter** jumps to a
slide, **B**/**W** blank to black/white, **S** shows presenter notes, **F** toggles
fullscreen, **R** resets the timer, **Escape** leaves. Click zones work too: left quarter
back, elsewhere forward.

# Export

**Export** writes the deck to **one self-contained `.html`** in the project's `exports/` —
every slide, beat, animation, morph, and font, playing in any web browser with the same keys
as Present mode. No Flux on the presenting machine, no network, nothing to install: open the
file, give the talk.

# Between figures and slides

**Send to deck…** (in Figure mode's Inspector) turns a figure into a slide;
**Send to canvas…** (in the Slide panel) turns a slide into a paper figure — it becomes
citable as `@fig-…` like any other. Both directions keep plots live.

# Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause → fix |
|---|---|
| The animation chords do nothing | The animator is closed → open it with **Animate ⏱** first |
| A morph target is listed but disabled | The plots aren't structurally compatible (different series/axes) → use a crossfade (exit + enter) instead |
| A track shows ⚠ | Its element was deleted → re-target or delete the track (it's kept so you can re-link) |
| Present shows placeholder "Title / Subtitle" text | The slide was created with a starter layout → delete the starters, or use the *blank* layout when composing by hand |
